title: Always On Top border crosses monitor and taskbar boundaries

status.label: Border clipping plan
status.detail: The reporter already answered the expected-behavior question: do not cross monitor boundaries or cover the taskbar. No author wait remains.

next_action.label: Validate border work-area clipping
next_action.reason: Exercise the existing reproduction on two monitors before changing overlay geometry.

judgment.rationale: The clarified expectation and screenshots identify the boundary defect. Current GetFrameRect expands DWM frame bounds by border thickness without clipping in that function; rendering-region behavior still needs verification.
evidence: 0.80.1 report supplies a two-monitor arrangement and visible border spill.
A maintainer added a taskbar-overlap screenshot and asked for intended behavior.
WindowBorder.cpp GetFrameRect expands all four frame edges by frameThickness.
Related closed reports #32735, #31941 and #32750 link back to this open report; no fix PR was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on mixed-DPI monitors, then approve a rendering clip that preserves borders for genuinely spanning windows.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report is a repository-owned border-rendering issue with answered requirements; related duplicate reports do not constitute a fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Clip Always On Top decoration to eligible monitor work areas
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the separate topmost border overlay uses frame bounds expanded by frameThickness, allowing decoration outside the pinned window's monitor work area.
plan: Reproduce edge/taskbar spill and trace GetFrameRect, WindowBorder::UpdateBorderProperties and FrameDrawer output in src/modules/alwaysontop/AlwaysOnTop.

Compute an explicit visible border region: clip to the containing monitor work area when the target is wholly on one monitor, and define a union of eligible work areas for spanning windows rather than arbitrarily selecting one monitor.
Apply clipping to rendering/overlay region without moving or resizing the target window; update it on window moves, DPI, taskbar and display changes.
Add geometry tests and multi-monitor UI checks for negative coordinates, auto-hide taskbars and thick borders.
verification: Pin a window flush with every edge of a monitor and verify no decoration appears on an adjacent monitor or over the taskbar.
Move the pinned window across two mixed-DPI monitors and verify spanning-window decoration, thickness, rounded corners and z-order remain correct.

confidence.rationale: Expanded frame geometry directly matches the screenshots, but the final clipping policy and current rendering behavior need an end-to-end test.

issue_context.summary: Always On Top's external border extends onto a neighboring display and over the taskbar when the pinned window is at an edge.
known_information: The original 0.80.1 report includes monitor arrangement and failure screenshots.
The July author reply supplied the requested expected behavior.
Status-Reproducible and Needs-Team-Response are present; the issue is unassigned.
inferences: An inflated overlay rectangle may need work-area-aware clipping; this remains a rendering hypothesis.
issue_context.analysis: The requested requirements are already supplied. Further progress belongs to maintainers reproducing boundary geometry, not another author-feedback request.
initial_investigation: Read the full report and all three comments, timeline-linked duplicates and related PR search.
Inspected upstream WindowBorder.cpp GetFrameRect and overlay SetWindowPos calls; the frame bounds are expanded before drawing.

actions.label: Test border at monitor and taskbar edges

prerequisites: Two physical monitors in the report's arrangement; also test different DPI scales.
Enable the Always On Top border and use a resizable test window.
steps: Pin the test window and place it entirely on one monitor, flush to the edge shared with the other monitor.
Inspect the adjacent display for border spill; repeat at the taskbar edge.
Repeat with a thicker border, then move the window so it genuinely spans both monitors.
Trace the inflated frame bounds and visible drawing region through display/DPI changes.
reproduce.expected_result: Decoration for a window wholly on one monitor stays on that monitor and outside the taskbar; spanning-window behavior remains coherent.

actions.label: Approve border clipping fix plan
actions.note: Confirm rendering behavior and spanning-window policy before implementing.
